name: Isotropic Residuum Propagation
definition: A technique to reduce propagation costs by switching to cheaper isotropic propagation once the radiance anisotropy falls below a threshold, merging grids into a single global grid.
summary: Isotropic Residuum Propagation accelerates light transport by merging directional grids into a single global grid once anisotropy drops, reducing computational cost while maintaining visual accuracy.
